item.title: Exchange Update Failures, Broadcom Router RCE, and OpenCode API Key Exposure
item.content:encoded:
Window: 19 Oct 06:00 → 19 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi Flaw Lets Attackers in Range Run Code as Root on Routers — Should Read

An unpatched flaw in Broadcom’s WPS implementation lets attackers within Wi‑Fi range send crafted setup frames and execute code as root on affected routers without knowing the network password. Millions of older and newer Broadcom-based devices may be exposed, with replacement often the only practical mitigation for unsupported models.

  • Researcher Quentin Kaiser disclosed that a flaw in Broadcom’s Wi-Fi Protected Setup software can allow an attacker within radio range to run code as root on affected routers without a Wi-Fi password or pairing step.
  • Kaiser demonstrated the flaw against Belgian provider gateways, reading the Wi-Fi password from an Orange Belgium Askey TCG3000 and opening a Wi-Fi-carried reverse shell on a Proximus Sagemcom BBOX3V+.
  • The vulnerable code affects older eCos-based Broadcom BCM3380, BCM3383, and BCM33834 chips as well as newer Linux-based BCM3390, BCM65xx, and BCM68xx families, potentially affecting millions of devices.
  • Kaiser says older eCos-based devices have no usable fix and may remain permanently vulnerable, while newer models could be fixed if manufacturers move to hostapd Wi-Fi software.
  • No CVE has been assigned and no patch has been deployed for the affected routers; Kaiser provides YARA rules and a live-access-point checking script as triage tools.

Technologies: router, iot-device

Products: bcm3380, bcm3383, bcm33834, bcm3390, bcm65xx, bcm68xx, tcg3000, bbox3v-plus, hostapd

Vendors: broadcom, askey, sagemcom

Microsoft: October Windows Server updates break Exchange sign-in, mail flow — Should Read

Microsoft says October 2026 Windows Server security updates can disrupt Outlook on the web sign-ins and mail delivery on some on-premises Exchange servers due to a new Endpoint Mapper memory limit. A temporary registry change raising the Endpoint Lookup call cap can mitigate the issue while Microsoft develops a fix.

  • Microsoft confirmed that October 2026 Windows Server security updates can cause Outlook on the web sign-in and mail delivery problems on some on-premises Exchange Server systems running Windows Server 2019 or later.
  • Affected users may be unable to access email, messages sent from Outlook may remain in the Outbox, and Exchange may have trouble accessing mailboxes during mailbox replication.
  • Microsoft said the update introduced a default limit of 512 simultaneous Endpoint Lookup calls, which may be insufficient for heavily loaded Exchange Server workloads.
  • Microsoft provided a temporary workaround that raises the Endpoint Mapper limit through the EpmapSavedContextCap registry value and requires rebooting the Exchange Server.
  • Microsoft said the issue is unrelated to October 2026 Exchange Server security updates and advised customers not to uninstall those updates.

Technologies: operating-system, email-security

Products: exchange-server, outlook-on-the-web, windows-server-2019, windows-server-2025

Vendors: microsoft

OpenCode Console Breach May Have Exposed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API Keys — Should Read

OpenCode says an intruder accessed a legacy Console system, potentially exposing OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API keys stored by 1.4% of Console users. Affected users should immediately revoke and replace provider keys and review their accounts for unauthorized usage.

  • OpenCode said an intruder accessed a legacy system connected to its optional Console service on the night of October 16, potentially exposing third-party AI provider keys saved there.
  • OpenCode said 1.4% of Console users were affected, all of whom had linked an outside provider, and it emailed them on October 17 to revoke and replace their keys.
  • The incident involved keys stored in OpenCode Console, while keys added locally to OpenCode’s command-line and desktop applications remain in a SQLite database on the user’s machine.
  • OpenCode advised affected users to review provider usage and billing for unauthorized requests, and some users reported charges they said they did not make.
  • OpenCode described the incident as ongoing and related to a large-scale model-distillation campaign, but did not disclose how the legacy system was accessed or whether any keys were copied or used.

Technologies: api-gateway, database

Products: opencode-console, opencode-cli, opencode-desktop, sqlite

Vendors: opencode, openai, anthropic, google

Proactively Defending Financial Institutions Against North Korean Remote IT Workers — Optional

North Korean operatives use legitimate or rented identities and domestic residential connections to secure remote IT jobs, allowing them to evade standard KYC and AML checks while routing salary payments back to North Korea. Financial institutions should analyze connection origins, payment-routing changes, and hiring anomalies before onboarding.

  • Silent Push identified a North Korean recruiting scheme on Discord in which a recruiter offered U.S., European Union, and Latin American citizens 35% of a salary to provide their identity and appear on job applications.
  • The remaining 65% of the salary is sent to the North Korean worker through cryptocurrency, wire transfers, or third-party payment processors.
  • The scheme can pass document-based KYC and AML checks because the identity is legitimate and the connection appears to come from a clean domestic residential IP address.
  • The operator may be located upstream of the residential address through a residential proxy or a KVM-over-IP relay in a laptop farm.
  • The report recommends that financial institutions examine where an applicant's connection begins, watch for early requests to redirect salary to an EMI or third-party account, and coordinate information sharing between HR and cybersecurity teams.

Technologies: proxy, remote-access

Vendors: silent-push

item.content:encoded:
Window: 18 Oct 18:00 → 18 Oct 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

OpenCode Security Breach: Distillation Attack Hit Console Users With Linked AI Providers. How to Find OpenCode on Developer Machines and Respond — Should Read

OpenCode disclosed an ongoing breach tied to a large-scale distillation attack affecting 1.4% of Console users with linked Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google providers. Organizations should identify developers using OpenCode, verify whether provider credentials were linked, and rotate relevant API keys while monitoring provider usage for unauthorized activity.

  • OpenCode disclosed an ongoing security breach on October 18, 2026, related to what it described as a large-scale distillation attack.
  • OpenCode said the incident affected 1.4% of OpenCode Console users who had linked external providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.
  • OpenCode stated that it emailed every affected user on the morning of October 18 and that users who did not receive an email were not impacted.
  • OpenCode has not published a root cause, a list of affected versions, or details about what data was accessed.
  • The article recommends that users with linked provider credentials rotate relevant API keys and review provider usage dashboards for unexpected requests.

Products: opencode, opencode-console, dev-machine-guard, threat-center

item.title: Active Exploitation of SiteGuard WAF CVE-2026-106931 Enables Root Command Execution
item.content:encoded:
Window: 18 Oct 14:00 → 18 Oct 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers exploit SiteGuard WAF flaw to run commands as admins — Must Read

Hackers are actively exploiting critical OS command-injection flaw CVE-2026-106931 in SiteGuard Server Edition’s default-enabled statistics feature to run commands as root or SYSTEM. Organizations should preserve diagnostic evidence and promptly apply the vendor’s updates or patches.

  • Hackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-106931, an OS command-injection flaw in the default-enabled statistics function of SiteGuard Server Edition.
  • Successful exploitation can allow attackers to execute commands with root or SYSTEM privileges on affected machines.
  • Affected releases include SiteGuard Server Edition for Apache httpd, Nginx, and IIS from version 2.20 up to before 8.00 Update 5, with separate affected FreeBSD releases up to before 7.00 Update 6.
  • SiteGuard provides updates and patches, including for end-of-life versions, and warns that remediation may erase attack traces.
  • The vendor advises administrators to download diagnostic information before applying updates or patches to preserve potential evidence.

Technologies: waf, web-server

Products: siteguard-server-edition, apache-httpd, nginx, internet-information-services

Vendors: eg-secure, apache-software-foundation, f5, microsoft

item.title: Phishing Email Abuses Trend Micro DKIM Relay to Pass DMARC
item.content:encoded:
Window: 18 Oct 10:00 → 18 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Security Vendor Hop Was on the Sender's Side — May Read

A phishing email reached a CEO’s inbox because the sender used Trend Micro Email Security as an outbound relay to generate an aligned DKIM signature, allowing DMARC to pass despite an SPF softfail. Security-vendor hops in email headers must be interpreted directionally: a vendor may be serving the sender, not protecting the recipient.

  • A phishing email targeting the CEO of a French calibration and metrology company passed DKIM, DMARC, and Microsoft composite authentication checks and was delivered to the Inbox with an SCL of 1.
  • Trend Micro Email Security acted as the sender’s outbound relay and signed the message using the sending domain’s DKIM key, rather than serving as an inbound security gateway for the recipient.
  • SPF softfailed because the sending domain did not authorize the Trend Micro relay IP, but DMARC still passed because the aligned DKIM signature passed.
  • The email contained a single PDF attachment with a raster QR code directing recipients to a subdomain of lunwah.com, with no clickable links, embedded files, forms, JavaScript, or auto-open action.
  • IRONSCALES classified the incident as phishing, identified the PDF as malicious and the display name as company impersonation, and quarantined the messages from both targeted mailboxes.

Technologies: email-security

Products: trend-micro-email-security, exchange-online-protection, adaptive-ai, themis

Vendors: trend-micro, microsoft, ironscales

item.title: ConnectWise Suspends Cloud Backup After Microsoft 365 Tenant Compromise
item.content:encoded:
Window: 18 Oct 06:00 → 18 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

ConnectWise Suspends Cloud Backup After Attackers Compromise Microsoft 365 Tenants — Must Read

ConnectWise disabled compromised application identities and suspended Cloud Backup after attackers used them to access Microsoft 365 tenants, potentially enabling persistent access through newly added application credentials. Customers should review Entra sign-ins, service principals, permissions, and mailbox rules for suspicious activity, especially from 144.172.64[.]128.

  • ConnectWise disabled seven application identities on October 17, 2026, after unknown threat actors obtained unauthorized access to them and compromised Microsoft 365 tenants.
  • ConnectWise revoked certificates for affected application connections and suspended Cloud Backup, leaving scheduled backups, archive access, and restoration unavailable while stating that existing archives remain encrypted, isolated, and preserved.
  • Huntress reported that it confirmed abuse of the ConnectWise Cloud Management Microsoft Teams application in one tenant and assessed that Exchange Online, Teams, and SharePoint applications were also targeted.
  • Huntress identified nearly 1,000 Entra tenants with sign-in activity from IP address 144.172.64[.]128, including about 300 successful sign-ins, although some lacked the required service principal for access.
  • Attackers could create new application credentials or assign elevated roles in affected tenants, allowing them to retain or expand access even after the original compromised credential is revoked.

Technologies: backup, cloud-platform, identity-provider, iam, casb

Products: connectwise-cloud-backup, connectwise-cloud-management, connectwise-saas-security, microsoft-365, microsoft-entra-id, exchange-online, microsoft-teams, sharepoint-online, microsoft-graph, microsoft-partner-center, azure-resource-manager

Vendors: connectwise, microsoft, huntress, skykick

item.title: MALFEX npm Malware and WordPress-Origin Phishing Abuse Trusted Infrastructure
item.content:encoded:
Window: 17 Oct 10:00 → 17 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

MALFEX npm Package 'imgdecode' Hides Shellcode Loader in Windows Native Addon — Should Read

The malicious npm package imgdecode is part of the MALFEX supply-chain campaign and uses a Windows native addon to download, decrypt, and inject shellcode into dllhost.exe. Developers who installed it or related packages should treat affected Windows systems as compromised and investigate persistence, stolen credentials, and cryptocurrency wallets.

  • The npm package imgdecode contains a compiled Windows addon that downloads encrypted shellcode from GitHub, decrypts it, and injects it into a new dllhost.exe process when loaded by a Node.js program.
  • Researchers link imgdecode to the MALFEX campaign, in which an unknown actor has published malicious npm packages targeting Windows systems since August 2023.
  • MALFEX packages have delivered Overlord RAT and a Node.js stealer called movinlike, which collects browser, messaging, cryptocurrency-wallet, gaming-app, and sensitive-file data.
  • The malware can receive remote commands to execute shell commands, transfer files, control processes, access the clipboard, capture screenshots, and control mouse and keyboard input.
  • Developers who installed the affected packages are advised to isolate potentially affected Windows systems, check persistence mechanisms, rotate credentials, and move cryptocurrency funds to new wallets if seed phrases were stored on the systems.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control, operating-system

Products: npm-registry, node-js, windows, github, imgdecode

Vendors: npm, github, microsoft, safedep

The Phishing Email That Carried Its Own Mailer's Path — May Read

A phishing email impersonating Israeli justice authorities passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC because attackers used a compromised WordPress site's legitimate hosting account and mail infrastructure to send it. Headers exposed the locally run malicious script in a hidden WordPress directory, while the lure avoided attachment sandboxing by linking to an MSI installer instead.

  • A Hebrew legal-proceedings phishing email impersonating Israeli authorities reached an accounting mailbox at a global pharmaceutical manufacturer despite passing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks.
  • Headers showed that the message was submitted locally through Exim by a script in randomly named directories under the compromised website's WordPress wp-includes/sitemaps directory.
  • The compromised domain's own hosting account, SPF-authorized outbound infrastructure, and DKIM key were used to send and sign the message, so its authentication results were valid before recipient-side rewriting.
  • The email claimed that an attachment required review but contained no attachment; instead, it linked to an unverified Windows installer named isrelherp.msi on a Cloudflare-fronted .es domain.
  • The recipient's secure email gateway and Safe Links rewriting altered the message body and caused later DKIM and DMARC failures, while the gateway's pre-rewrite results showed the original message had passed authentication.

Technologies: cms, email-security, cloud-platform

Products: wordpress, cpanel, exim, exchange-online, microsoft-safe-links, ironscales

Vendors: wordpress-project, cpanel, exim-project, microsoft, cloudflare, ironscales

item.title: Compromised ConnectWise Credential Accesses 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants
item.content:encoded:
Window: 17 Oct 06:00 → 17 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers Use Compromised ConnectWise Credential to Sign In to 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants — Must Read

A compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credential was used to access 173 Microsoft 365 customer tenants, potentially exposing email, files, Teams data, and directory information through the app’s broad permissions. Organizations using the app should disable it, investigate Entra service-principal and audit logs, and review newly added application credentials until ConnectWise completes credential rotation.

  • Unknown threat actors used a compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup Microsoft 365 credential to obtain Microsoft Graph tokens and sign in to 173 partner or customer tenants.
  • ConnectWise Cloud Backup has broad access to Microsoft 365 data, including mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, and directory data, so its compromised credential could provide comparable access in each tenant where the app was installed.
  • Huntress observed activity from IP address 144.172.64.128 on October 15, with the actor moving through tenants in sorted GUID order within seconds, suggesting scripted targeting.
  • In one partner tenant, a separate ConnectWise Cloud Management app for Microsoft Teams added itself to the Global Administrator role and added new client secrets to two other trusted applications.
  • ConnectWise closed Cloud Backup application access until further notice, said it found no evidence that partner backup data was compromised, and advised customers to review relevant Microsoft Entra service-principal sign-in logs.

Technologies: backup, cloud-platform, identity-provider, iam

Products: connectwise-cloud-backup, connectwise-cloud-management-for-microsoft-teams, microsoft-365, microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-graph, aomei-backupper, huntress-security-platform

Vendors: connectwise, microsoft, aomei, huntress

item.title: Generative AI Accelerates Ransomware Operations After Initial Access
item.content:encoded:
Window: 16 Oct 22:00 → 17 Oct 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

Ransomware at Machine Speed: How GenAI Shrinks the Path after Initial Access — Optional

Generative AI is helping ransomware operators create more convincing phishing lures, rapidly identify valuable data after initial access, and generate varied custom scripts that evade signature-based detection. Defenders must apply AI-driven detection and zero-trust controls alongside tested security practices to keep pace.

  • Ransomware operators can use generative AI to produce polished, target-language phishing messages, websites, and other social-engineering material.
  • After gaining access to a victim system, attackers can use generative AI to search and classify accessible data to identify sensitive or valuable material for theft or encryption.
  • Generative AI can help attackers rapidly create and revise custom scripts and malware, varying signatures and making signature-based detection more difficult.
  • Custom tools created with generative AI may make less-resourced ransomware operators harder to distinguish from larger, well-funded threat groups.
  • Defenders can use AI-enabled detection, zero-trust telemetry, and automated response workflows to detect, investigate, and respond to ransomware threats more quickly.

Technologies: proxy, browser, soar

Products: agentic-secops, secure-web-gateway, zero-trust-browser

Vendors: zscaler

item.title: Actively Exploited NetScaler CVE-2026-88771 and Critical Magento BlockStrap RCE
item.content:encoded:
Window: 16 Oct 18:00 → 16 Oct 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

CVE-2026-88771: Inside the Exploitation of a Critical NetScaler RCE Vulnerability — Must Read

CVE-2026-88771 is a critical, actively exploited unauthenticated RCE in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway that attackers use to poison logs, execute commands, and install web shells or FreeBSD payloads. Organizations should preserve evidence, hunt for indicators, isolate suspected devices, rotate exposed secrets, and upgrade immediately to Citrix’s fixed builds.

  • Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-88771 on September 27, 2026, a critical NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway flaw that allows unauthenticated attackers to run arbitrary commands on affected appliances.
  • Citrix confirmed exploitation of unmitigated appliances, and CISA added CVE-2026-88771 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of active exploitation worldwide.
  • ThreatLabz observed attackers place Base64-encoded payloads in HTTP access logs, then use forged NetScaler PPE failure messages to cause a privileged script to decode and execute those payloads.
  • Observed payloads attempted to create PHP and Perl web shells, alter the Apache configuration to enable PHP and Perl CGI handling, and download and execute a FreeBSD x64 binary.
  • Citrix recommends upgrading NetScaler ADC and Gateway to fixed builds, while the article advises preserving forensic evidence and investigating potentially affected appliances before updating.

Technologies: load-balancer, vpn, remote-access, cms

Products: netscaler-adc, netscaler-gateway, adobe-commerce, magento-open-source, zscaler-private-access

Vendors: citrix, zscaler, adobe

Critical BlockStrap flaw lets hackers run code on Magento servers — Must Read

A critical Magento and Adobe Commerce flaw, CVE-2026-103849 (“BlockStrap”), can enable arbitrary PHP code execution through email-template directive injection. Administrators should apply Adobe’s October 2026 release or isolated patch and retain the separate September StyleSmuggler hotfix.

  • CVE-2026-103849, dubbed BlockStrap, is a maximum-severity flaw in Magento and Adobe Commerce that could allow arbitrary PHP code execution on store servers.
  • Sansec said it had not observed attacks exploiting BlockStrap but identified four potential attack paths in less than 24 hours and expects threat actors to find a way to exploit it.
  • The issue affects September versions of Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source through 2.4.9, plus Adobe Commerce B2B through 1.5.3.
  • Adobe’s October 13 bulletin describes the flaw as improper handling of special template-engine elements that can lead to arbitrary code execution.
  • Sansec advises administrators to apply Adobe’s October 2026 release or isolated patch and keep the separate September VULN-39341 StyleSmuggler hotfix installed.

Technologies: cms

Products: magento-open-source, adobe-commerce, adobe-commerce-b2b

Vendors: adobe, sansec

Web Scanning in Censys ASM Just Got Deeper — Optional

Censys ASM now fully renders JavaScript-driven web pages, follows complete redirect chains, captures screenshots, and maps web technologies to detect more than 400 web-specific CVE risks. The update aims to give organizations continuous visibility into the real, browser-rendered state of their external web attack surface.

  • Censys ASM now automatically performs full page loading and evaluates the browser-built version of web pages, enabling visibility into content that is not present in an initial server response.
  • The updated web scanning maps JavaScript libraries, web technologies, and plugins across an environment and flags associated vulnerabilities and risks.
  • Censys ASM adds more than 400 web-specific CVE detections for vulnerable libraries and outdated plugins.
  • The platform automatically captures a screenshot of every web entity in an inventory within 24 hours of discovery.
  • Censys ASM follows complete URL redirect chains so users can identify the final destination, including potentially hijacked domains or phishing sites.

Products: censys-asm, jquery, angularjs, wordpress, hugo, react, angular, vue, next-js

Vendors: censys, jquery, angular, wordpress, hugo, react, vue, vercel
